newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Analysts welcome De Boer merger.
newsitem.headline: Analysts welcome De Boer merger.

text.p: A planned merger between regional supermarkets chain De Boer Winkelbedrijven and unlisted sector rival Unigro will generate clear synergy benefits, analysts said in an initial reaction on Wednesday.
"There is tremendous scope for cost savings running into tens of millions of guilders," said Heinie Hakker, retail analyst with Barclays de Zoete Wedd.

The merger of the two companies, both mid-sized players on the Dutch food retail market, would enable economies of scale in distribution and create the required critical mass to justify costly investments in electronic customer cards, he said.
"Retailing is becoming more and more technologically driven, but the investments required are considerable," Hakker said.
Analysts said the merger was also a good geographical fit. De Boer was stronger in the northern Netherlands, where it gave Dutch market leader Ahold a good run for its money.

Unigro, founded in the southern Dutch town of Breda in 1925, was strongest in the south. In addition it derived some 20 percent of turnover from the fast-growing Spanish groceries market, where it was one of the top ten players.
A further 20 percent of sales are booked on the Belgian market.
"Unigro has had some pretty lean years though," said an analyst who declined to be named.

He said restructuring had virtually halved the company's net profits to 25.2 million guilders in the 1995/96 fiscal year ending January 31 from some 47 million guiders two years earlier. But he added the reorganisation looked to be starting to bear fruit.
Unigro and De Boer were both working on improving distribution, but Unigro appeared to have booked more progress, he added.

Analysts said that based on the information available prior to a corporate briefing later on Wednesday they expected the combine to book earnings per share of some nine guilders in 1997, up from an estimated 8.40 guilders for De Boer currently.
"Basically it looks like a good deal," the analyst said.
"I did rate De Boer a Sell but I will be reviewing my recommendation."
-- Lien van der Leij, A'dam newsroom +31 20 504 5000
